rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It is an immediately preceding Eisenhower resignation-acceptance letter with the same sequence: regret at departure, reassurance derived from the official's abilities and service, praise tied to four years of work, thanks, and satisfaction that the official will remain available. The unusually close wording around “constant reassurance,” “many abilities,” devotion, and future service is stronger than generic resignation-letter similarity. C11 and C12 share the broader structure but substantially less distinctive language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have been reassured by the knowledge that you were devoting your many abilities to the strengthening of the civil service
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have drawn constant reassurance from the fact that your many abilities were devoted to the vital task of preparing our nation
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel construction combining reassurance, the official's “many abilities,” and those abilities being devoted to a governmental mission.

shared_material.child_excerpt: you have contributed immeasurably to the achievement of our purpose... your outstanding service
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The nation has indeed profited by your dedication to this service over the past four years.
shared_material.explanation: Both credit four years of dedicated service with materially advancing an important governmental objective.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am grateful, too, that you are willing to be of further service in the future.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am glad that you can continue as a member of the Committee and will be available for further consultations from time to time.
shared_material.explanation: Both close the substantive portion by expressing gratitude that the departing official will remain available for future service.
